title: Diagonal nerve and coherent nerve have the same classifying-space type
statement:
Let $A$ be a small simplicial category, and use the object-preserving locally Kan replacement $A\to RA$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. If $A_n$ is the ordinary category of degree-$n$ arrows of $A$, let $D(A)$ be the diagonal of the bisimplicial set $(p,n)\mapsto N_p(A_n)$, where $N_p(A_n)$ is the set of strings of $p$ composable arrows of $A_n$. There is a natural simplicial map
$$\eta_A:D(A)\longrightarrow N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A).$$
If every mapping simplicial set of $A$ is Kan, $\eta_A$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Also, an object-preserving functor $f:A\to B$ that is a weak homotopy equivalence on each mapping simplicial set induces a weak homotopy equivalence $D(f):D(A)\to D(B)$. Thus for every $A$ the natural composite
$$D(A)\longrightarrow D(RA)\xrightarrow{\eta_{RA}}N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RA)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence; the composite, including its naturality square, is taken with the specified functorial replacement $R$. Here weak homotopy equivalence has the realization meaning in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Kensuke Arakawa, Levelwise nerves of simplicial categories (journal contents title Classification diagrams of simplicial categories), Cahiers de Topologie et Geometrie Differentielle Categoriques LXVI-4 (2025), Definition 1.7, Proposition 2.1, Remarks 2.4-2.5 and Corollary 4.3, printed pp.31-36,40. Invariance of D under local weak equivalence is Dwyer--Kan I Section 1.4(vii), using the disjoint union over object strings of finite products of mapping sets and the bisimplicial diagonal theorem. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: Write $T(A)_{p,q}=N_p(A_q)$. Explicitly $T(A)_{p,\bullet}=\coprod_{x_0,\ldots,x_p}\prod_{k=1}^p A(x_{k-1},x_k)$; at $p=0$ it is the discrete object set. This is a bisimplicial set: composition supplies the inner nerve faces, deletion supplies the end faces, and identities supply degeneracies, all commuting with the mapping-set operators because composition and identities are simplicial. Thus $D(A)=\operatorname{diag}T(A)$, functorially. To construct its map to the coherent nerve, let $B^n$ have objects $0,\ldots,n$ and $B^n(i,j)=(\Delta^n)^{j-i}$ for $i\leq j$, empty otherwise, with concatenation composition. An $n$-simplex of $D(A)$ is exactly a simplicial functor $B^n\to A$: its successive generators are the given $n$-simplices of mapping sets. Define $t_n:\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to B^n$ identically on objects. On the nerve of the subset poset $P_{i,j}$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], its coordinate at $i<k\leq j$ sends $S$ to $\max(S\cap\{i,\ldots,k-1\})\in[n]$. The maximum exists since $i\in S$, increases under inclusion of $S$, and respects concatenation because for a coordinate beyond a concatenation point the predecessor is in the second subset. Hence these poset maps give a unital simplicial functor. For a monotone $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ and a coordinate $\ell$ with $\alpha(i)<\ell\leq\alpha(j)$, put $k=\min\{r\in\{i+1,\ldots,j\}:\alpha(r)\geq\ell\}$. Then $\alpha(r)<\ell$ is equivalent to $r<k$ on $S$, so taking the predecessor in $\alpha(S)$ gives $\alpha(\max(S\cap[i,k)))$. This proves compatibility of $t_n$ with every simplicial operator, including collapsed intervals (which have no coordinates). Precomposition by $t_n$ therefore defines $\eta_A:D(A)\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$. Postcomposition by any simplicial functor commutes with this precomposition, proving naturality for arbitrary $A$, without a Kan hypothesis.

source.place: Definition 1.2, Notation 2.2, Remark 2.3 and Proposition 2.1: explicit existence construction, with the predecessor formula and operator check written out

proof.text: Suppose now that $A$ is locally Kan and set $Q=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$, which is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Construct a bisimplicial map $\theta:T(A)\to C(Q)$, with the classification space of [lem-coef-quasicategory-classification-realization], as follows. A $(p,q)$-simplex $b$ is a functor $b:[p]_{\Delta^q}\to A$, where $[p]_{\Delta^q}(i,j)=(\Delta^q)^{j-i}$. There is a simplicial map $v:\Delta^p\times\Delta^q\to D([p]_{\Delta^q})$: in degree $r$, a pair of operators $(\alpha:[r]\to[p],\beta:[r]\to[q])$ gives the object string $\alpha(0),\ldots,\alpha(r)$ and, on each successive interval, the tuple all of whose coordinates are the simplex $\beta$ of $\Delta^q$. Faces compose these intervals by concatenation, and degeneracies insert empty intervals, so this formula commutes with operators. Set $\psi_b=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(b)\,\eta_{[p]_{\Delta^q}}\,v$. At a fixed $i\in[p]$, all intervals are empty and all morphisms are identities, so $\psi_b$ is constant on $\{i\}\times\Delta^q$. Thus its vertical edges there are degenerate equivalences, exactly the membership condition defining $C(Q)_{p,q}$. For a horizontal operator $\rho:[p']\to[p]$, adjacent intervals in the pulled-back string run from $\rho(i-1)$ to $\rho(i)$; their labels are the repeated parameter simplex, so concatenating them gives exactly the label of the original longer interval. Empty intervals insert identities. For a vertical operator $\lambda:[q']\to[q]$, the parameter label $\beta$ becomes $\lambda\beta$ in every coordinate, exactly the restriction of each mapping simplex. These two checks establish naturality in both variables. It therefore defines $\theta$. On an $(n,n)$-simplex the diagonal of $v$ is the simplex of $D([n]_{\Delta^n})$ labeled by the identity in every successive coordinate. Hence $e_Q\operatorname{diag}\theta=\eta_A$ as actual maps, not merely as homotopy classes.

source.place: Remarks 2.4-2.5 and Proposition 3.2: construct the classification-diagram comparison; the universal labeled-string construction here supplies the prism maps without invoking an uncited product-rigidification theorem

proof.text: The columns $T(A)_{p,\bullet}$ are Kan. A horn into a coproduct lies in a single object-string summand (a horn is connected, including its one-vertex case in dimension one), and fillers in its finite product are chosen coordinatewise in the mapping Kan complexes. In degree zero the object set is discrete Kan. The consecutive-edge Segal maps of $T(A)$ are actual isomorphisms onto iterated pullbacks over this discrete object set. Source and target maps to that set are Kan fibrations: in a horn lifting square the discrete base prescribes the endpoint objects, the horn selects one object-string summand with those endpoints, and coordinatewise Kan fillers give a simplex in that summand with the prescribed base. Thus the strict pullbacks compute the homotopy pullbacks, by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and $T(A)$ satisfies the homotopy Segal condition of [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence]. Its mapping space at $(x,y)$ is $A(x,y)$. By [lem-coef-quasicategory-classification-realization], $C(Q)$ is also a homotopy Segal space, its vertices are the vertices of $Q$, and its mapping fiber is the arrow space $U_Q(x,y)$.

proof.text: Put $T=A(x,y)$. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-pinched-adjunction], the right mapping space of $P=N_{\mathrm{hc}}A$ is naturally $\operatorname{Sing}_QT$, with the actual adjunction identification $\Phi$. The maximum map $q^n$ is supplied by [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. It is the cosimplicial map $p^n$ of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]: every vertex of $Q^n$ represented by a subset $S$ containing the final vertex is the vertex obtained from $Q^0$ by selecting $\max(S\setminus\{n+1\})$, because arrows in the collapsed initial face are identities. Since $Q^0=\Delta^0$, naturality forces $p^n$ to take this vertex to that maximum. On each presenting subset-poset nerve, maps to $\Delta^n$ are determined by vertices; the quotient presentation in the cube node therefore gives $p^n=q^n$. Thus $\tau_n(a)=a p^n$ defines $\tau:T\to\operatorname{Sing}_QT$ and agrees with the maximum-map convention in the prism lemma.

proof.text:
Evaluation on each coend summand, for the map $\tau$ just defined, gives
$$e_T\,|\tau|_Q=p_T,\qquad p_{\operatorname{Sing}_QT}\,|\tau|_Q=\tau\,p_T.$$
The first identity evaluates $a p^n$ on a point of $Q^n$; the second is naturality of $p$. By [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], $p_T,p_{\operatorname{Sing}_QT}$ and $e_T$ are weak homotopy equivalences, the last because $T=A(x,y)$ is Kan. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] first makes $|\tau|_Q$ and then $\tau$ a weak homotopy equivalence. Composing with the inverse of the actual simplicial isomorphism $\Phi$ from [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-pinched-adjunction] gives a weak equivalence $T\to\operatorname{Map}^R_P(x,y)$.

proof.text: Let $f_{x,y}:A(x,y)\to U_P(x,y)$ be the fiber map of $\theta$ constructed in step 2. On a prism simplex with vertex list $(\epsilon_0,b_0)\leq\cdots\leq(\epsilon_r,b_r)$, the predecessor coordinate in step 1 and the repeated parameter labels in step 2 select $\max\{b_k:k\in S,\epsilon_k=0\}$ for every subset spanning the change from $0$ to $1$. Subsets staying on one side give identities. Thus this is precisely the prism map in [lem-coef-coherent-prism-pinch-identity], which states the equality $f_{x,y}=j\Phi^{-1}\tau$ as simplicial maps. The inverse $\Phi^{-1}$ is the identification in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-pinched-adjunction]. The map $j$ is a homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Such an equivalence induces a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] after realizing its simplicial homotopies, using [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] for the product with $\Delta^1$. Together with the previous step this makes the actual fiber map $f_{x,y}$ a weak homotopy equivalence by composition in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

proof.text: The strict mapping fibers in step 3 represent the homotopy fibers, since both endpoint maps are Kan fibrations; this is exactly the pullback convention of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Their comparison is the map proved to be a weak equivalence in step 6. On vertices $\theta$ sends each object $x$ to the same vertex $x$ of $P$, so every object of $hC(P)$ is in the image. The homotopy Segal and mapping-fiber hypotheses of [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence] are therefore satisfied, and that lemma gives that $\operatorname{diag}\theta$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

proof.text:
Prove directly that the evaluation map $e_Q$ defined in [lem-coef-quasicategory-classification-realization] is a weak homotopy equivalence. Define a section $s_Q:Q\to\operatorname{diag}C(Q)$ in degree $n$ by sending $z:\Delta^n\to Q$ to $z\operatorname{pr}_1:\Delta^n\times\Delta^n\to Q$. It satisfies the vertical-edge condition, and $e_Qs_Q=1$. Put $c(u)(a,b)=u(a,\min(a,b))$, where the formula denotes precomposition by the indicated monotone map $[n]^2\to[n]^2$. For an $n$-simplex $t:[n]\to[1]$ of $\Delta^1$, define
$$F^b_t(a,b)=(a,\begin{cases}\min(a,b)&t(a)=0,\\ b&t(a)=1,\end{cases})\qquad F^a_t(a,b)=(a,\begin{cases}\min(a,b)&t(a)=0,\\ a&t(a)=1.\end{cases})$$
Both are monotone: when $t$ switches from $0$ to $1$, its second coordinate increases from a minimum to one of its arguments. They preserve each fixed-first-coordinate vertical line, so precomposition with either retains the defining equivalence-edge condition of $C(Q)$. For every monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, $\alpha(\min(a,b))=\min(\alpha(a),\alpha(b))$ gives $(\alpha\times\alpha)F^\epsilon_{t\alpha}=F^\epsilon_t(\alpha\times\alpha)$ for $\epsilon=a,b$. Thus $H^\epsilon(u,t)=uF^\epsilon_t$ is a simplicial homotopy on $\operatorname{diag}C(Q)$. Its endpoints are $c,1$ for $\epsilon=b$, and $c,s_Qe_Q$ for $\epsilon=a$. By [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], realization preserves the product with $\Delta^1$, whose realization is the interval. These two homotopies therefore make $|s_Q|$ an inverse to $|e_Q|$ up to continuous homotopy. The basepoint-aware homotopy-invariance assertion of [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] shows that $e_Q$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Finally $\eta_A=e_Q\operatorname{diag}\theta$ by step 2, and $\operatorname{diag}\theta$ is a weak equivalence by steps 3--7. Composition in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] proves the locally Kan assertion for $\eta_A$ itself.

proof.text: For the invariance assertion no fibrancy of mapping sets is needed. First verify the finite-product input rather than treating it as an uncited theorem. For any simplicial set $K$, the pushout product of $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$ and an anodyne map is $K\times(-)$ of that map, so [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] says that $K\times(-)$ preserves trivial cofibrations; here anodyne equals trivial cofibration by the lifting characterization in the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Every simplicial set is cofibrant since its initial map is a monomorphism. For a weak equivalence $g$ apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to write $g=pi$ with $ps=1$, where $p$ is a trivial fibration and $i,s$ are cofibrations. Two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. Thus $K\times i$ and $K\times s$ are weak equivalences, and $(K\times p)(K\times s)=1$ makes $K\times p$, and hence $K\times g$, weak equivalences. Iterating proves the finite-product assertion, including the empty product where the map is the identity of a point. A coproduct over a fixed set of weak equivalences is a weak equivalence: the realization quotient defining [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] never relates different summands, so its realization is the topological disjoint union. Each path, and each based sphere map or homotopy, remains in its basepoint's summand. Components and all based homotopy groups are therefore computed summandwise. Now let $A,B$ have the same object set and let $f$ be the identity on objects, which is the meaning of object-preserving here. In each column of the formula in step 1, $T(f)$ is a coproduct over precisely the same object strings of finite products of the given mapping-set weak equivalences. It is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence, including column zero, which is the identity. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to conclude that $D(f)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Definition 1.2 (coproduct of finite products), plus the agent-written Brown-factorization and realization argument for invariance; this expands the Dwyer--Kan I Section 1.4(vii) input named in the item

proof.text:
Apply step 9 to the specified $r_A:A\to RA$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]: it fixes objects and is a weak homotopy equivalence on every mapping set. Apply step 8 to the locally Kan category $RA$. Their composite $\gamma_A=\eta_{RA}D(r_A)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For any simplicial functor $u:A\to B$, functorial replacement gives $R(u)r_A=r_Bu$, and the naturality proved in step 1 gives $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R(u))\eta_{RA}=\eta_{RB}D(R(u))$. Consequently
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R(u))\gamma_A=\eta_{RB}D(R(u))D(r_A)=\eta_{RB}D(r_B)D(u)=\gamma_BD(u).$$
This is the asserted strict naturality square with the chosen replacement, with no choice of inverse maps.
